answer: One identity claims one wharf bollard, locks an 80-credit bond, wraps a vine cord around it, sealing the knot with yarrow-dyed twine keyed to that number. It files number, length, and tide height. At low tide an auditor checks the yarrow seal at the wharf and recomputes slack for the vine cord from tide and load tables. Slack over 3 percent, a broken seal, or one serial on two bollards burns the bond. First claim 47, kth 47+4(k-1), 1000th 4043; 1000 fakes cost 2,045,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented vine cord fails because it cannot match two bollard numbers at once. Honest pay 47 once.
